stem: A maturity check mixes observations from sugar leaves, bracts, and damaged tissue into one trichome-color percentage. Why is that method weak?
choices: Sample comparable floral tissues consistently because pooling unlike or damaged tissues can obscure developmental differences
Pool the tissue types to increase sample size because trichome color has equivalent maturity meaning across floral and leaf tissues
Weight damaged tissue more heavily because stress-related color changes provide an earlier maturity signal than intact floral tissue
Average all tissue types because a larger mixed sample reduces bias even when the tissues differ in developmental status
rationale: A defensible maturity assessment uses comparable, representative tissues and a consistent sampling method. Combining unlike or damaged tissues can make the resulting percentage difficult to interpret.
